D1.text: When the case allows, colchicine first for an acute gout flare.

D2.text: Prefers a written individual flare plan in advance.

D3.text: When a patient reports a side effect, first clarifies the timing between the symptom and the doses.

D4.text: When information is missing, asks about past experience with the drug.

D1.text: When the case allows, an NSAID (naproxen) first for an acute gout flare.

D2.text: Prefers the patient to call first, then confirm the plan.

D3.text: When a patient reports a side effect, first reviews the full medication list and recent changes.

D4.text: When information is missing, asks about other conditions and other medicines.

D1.text: For an acute gout flare, the regimen that worked and was tolerated before.

D2.text: Uses the existing individual plan when one exists and fits.

D3.text: When a patient reports a side effect, first asks whether the same reaction happened before.

D4.text: When information is missing, confirms the current prescription and existing plan.
